searchText: can client teams chime in / give a 👍 on this please? <@412614104222531604> I try to understand how bootnodes work with kurtosis. Could you confirm that, if there is let's say 3 Geth/Prysm couples: - `cl-1-prysm-geth` won't use the `--bootstrap-node` flag - `cl-2-prysm-geth` will use the `--bootstrap-node` flag with the ENR corresponding to `cl-1-prysm-geth` - `cl-3-prysm-geth` will use the `--bootstrap-node` flag with the ENR corresponding to `cl-1-prysm-geth` and `cl-2-prysm-geth` ? yes that’s how it works every participant n will get the enrs of all the previous participants (up to 20 bootnodes) except the first participant that will have no bootnode Oki thanks. What I'm trying to do: 1. I start 2 super nodes (node 1 and node 2) and 1 full node (node 3). 2. I immediately stop the full node (`docker stop`) 3. I wait for a few epochs 4. I restart the full node (`docker start`) Let's imagine during step 3, ENRs of node 1 and node 2 changed. Then, when I restart node 3, it will try to connect to node 1 and 2, but with the old ENR right? (So node 3 won't find any peer.) Yes exactly, docker stop/start won't change the runtime parameters of what kurtosis started the network with. So it'll try to peer with the old ENR. the ip/port won’t change so you should still be able to peer with using the old enr. Otherwise you should set a static enr entry will do now made a PR https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3908

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
<@412614104222531604> I try to understand how bootnodes work with kurtosis.
Could you confirm that, if there is let's say 3 Geth/Prysm couples:
- `cl-1-prysm-geth` won't use the `--bootstrap-node` flag
- `cl-2-prysm-geth` will use the `--bootstrap-node` flag with the ENR corresponding to `cl-1-prysm-geth`
- `cl-3-prysm-geth` will use the `--bootstrap-node` flag with the ENR corresponding to `cl-1-prysm-geth` and `cl-2-prysm-geth` 

?

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: every participant n will get the enrs of all the previous participants (up to 20 bootnodes)

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: except the first participant that will have no bootnode

Oki thanks.

What I'm trying to do:
1. I start 2 super nodes (node 1 and node 2) and 1 full node (node 3).
2. I immediately stop the full node (`docker stop`)
3. I wait for a few epochs
4. I restart the full node (`docker start`)

Let's imagine during step 3, ENRs of node 1 and node 2 changed.
Then, when I restart node 3, it will try to connect to node 1 and 2, but with the old ENR right?

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: Yes exactly, docker stop/start won't change the runtime parameters of what kurtosis started the network with. So it'll try to peer with the old ENR.
